=={{header|Omegese}}==
{{works with|omc|sha256 2c824805, aien-dev/omega-mv e5b32567, Linux AArch64}}
Omega has no imports, so the small output helpers (<code>emit</code> and friends) are part of the program.
<syntaxhighlight lang="text">
om2
text nl "\n"
text sp " "
text em "M"
text hdr "Mersenne primes 2^p - 1 for p <= 63, by the Lucas-Lehmer test:"
note w 0 and w 1 hold the high and low 64 bits of the last 128-bit product
global w ulong 2
note emit writes every byte of a to stdout; a short write is retried, an error exits 1
fn emit a view uchar * to void
o = ulong 0
while lt o len a bound 4096
k = write 1 a o sub len a o
if le k 0
exit 1
end
o = add o ulong k
end
end
note emitu writes n in decimal; 20 digits hold every ulong
fn emitu n ulong to void
d = new uchar 20 0
i = ulong 20
v = n
while true bound 20
i = sub i 1
put d i uchar add rem v 10 48
v = div v 10
if eq v 0
break
end
end
emit part d i sub 20 i
end
note mul128 forms a * b exactly from four 32 x 32 -> 64-bit partial products
fn mul128 a ulong b ulong to void
al = and a 0xffffffff
ah = shr a 32
bl = and b 0xffffffff
bh = shr b 32
ll = mul al bl
lh = mul al bh
hl = mul ah bl
hi = add mul ah bh shr lh 32
hi = add hi shr hl 32
mid = add shr ll 32 and lh 0xffffffff
mid = add mid and hl 0xffffffff
put w 1 add and ll 0xffffffff shl mid 32
put w 0 add hi shr mid 32
end
note sqm is s * s mod m for m = 2^p - 1, 2 < p <= 63,, s < m: the product x = q * 2^p + r folds to q + r
note x < 2^(2p), so q < 2^p and q + r < 2^64; a second fold and one subtraction finish it
fn sqm s ulong p ulong m ulong to ulong
mul128 s s
q = or shl get w 0 sub 64 p shr get w 1 p
t = add q and get w 1 m
t = add and t m shr t p
if ge t m
t = sub t m
end
ret t
end
note p is prime by trial division (p <= 63)
fn smallp p ulong to bool
if lt p 2
ret false
end
d = ulong 2
while le mul d d p bound 8
if eq rem p d 0
ret false
end
d = add d 1
end
ret true
end
note Lucas-Lehmer for odd prime p: s = 4, then p - 2 times s = s^2 - 2 mod M; M is prime iff s ends at 0
fn lltest p ulong to bool
m = sub shl ulong 1 p 1
s = ulong 4
for i ulong sub p 2
s = sqm s p m
if ge s 2
s = sub s 2
else
s = sub add s m 2
end
end
ret eq s 0
end
fn main to int
emit hdr
emit nl
note M2 = 3 is prime by definition; the test as stated covers odd prime p
emit em
emitu 2
p = ulong 3
while le p 63 bound 61
if smallp p
if lltest p
emit sp
emit em
emitu p
end
end
p = add p 2
end
emit nl
ret 0
end
</syntaxhighlight>
{{out}}
<pre>
Mersenne primes 2^p - 1 for p &lt;= 63, by the Lucas-Lehmer test:
M2 M3 M5 M7 M13 M17 M19 M31 M61
</pre>
